name: Hiddenite
physical: Traditionally associated with a refreshed feeling
Said to bring a gentle, calming sense of ease
Crystal healers link it with relaxation of chest tension
summary: Hiddenite is the rare green gem of spodumene, first found in North Carolina, a soft-hearted stone linked in crystal lore with compassion and renewal.
intro: Hiddenite is the green to yellow-green variety of spodumene, coloured by traces of chromium, and it is one of the rarest gems in the world. Unlike its pink cousin kunzite, hiddenite tends to occur in smaller crystals, often less than a few carats when cut, which makes large clean stones remarkable. The best colour is a clear, grassy emerald green, though many stones are paler. Like kunzite, hiddenite has strong pleochroism and perfect cleavage, so it is delicate. Because of its rarity and its link with a famous American locality, hiddenite is treasured by collectors of rare gems and by those who appreciate gentle heart-chakra stones.
history: Hiddenite was discovered in 1879 in Alexander County, North Carolina, and was first thought to be emerald. The mineralogist J. Lawrence Smith recognised it as a green variety of spodumene and named it in honour of William Earl Hidden, a mineral collector and geologist who had been searching for platinum in the area. The North Carolina deposits, around the town now called Hiddenite, have been mined by hobbyists and collectors ever since. Some green spodumene from Brazil and Afghanistan is also sold under the name, though true chromium-bearing hiddenite is scarce. It is the town's namesake and a prized rarity in gem circles.
meaning: In crystal tradition hiddenite is a gentle heart stone that encourages compassion, openness and peaceful relationships. Practitioners link it with the heart chakra and say it can help a person feel safe enough to share feelings, while keeping a sense of balance. Its green colour suggests renewal, and it is often used for fresh starts in love or friendship. Some use it to feel connected with the natural world and with a quiet, hopeful state of mind. Because it is rare, it is also considered a precious personal talisman. Physically it is traditionally associated with a refreshed, calmer feeling in the chest, as a symbolic support rather than a treatment.
howToUse: Wear hiddenite as a pendant close to the heart on days when you want to be gently open. Hold a piece in meditation and breathe slowly, picturing a soft green glow around your chest. Keep a small stone in your pocket when you have a conversation that needs patience. Pair it with kunzite for a spodumene duo that balances love and renewal, or with rose quartz for tenderness. If you cannot get hiddenite, green kunzite-like material or prehnite can serve similar roles.
care: Hiddenite is brittle with cleavage and can chip or split with knocks, so handle it gently. Clean with lukewarm water and a soft cloth, avoiding ultrasonic and steam cleaners. Keep it out of strong sunlight and heat, as the colour can fade. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or selenite. Store each stone in a soft pouch or padded box, away from harder gems, and set it in protective jewelry such as pendants rather than rings.
identify: True hiddenite is green spodumene with chromium colour, strong pleochroism and perfect cleavage. Look-alikes include emerald, tsavorite, green tourmaline, peridot, green fluorite and glass. Many stones sold as hiddenite are actually irradiated or heat-treated kunzite-family stones that appear green, though these can fade. Real chrome-coloured hiddenite is very rare. Ask for the origin and any treatment, and request a lab report for high-priced pieces to confirm that the stone is natural spodumene.

faq.a: Hiddenite is the green variety of spodumene, coloured by chromium. It was discovered in North Carolina in 1879 and is much rarer than its pink cousin, kunzite.
In crystal tradition it supports compassion, openness and gentle renewal. It is a heart chakra stone, often chosen to help the wearer feel balanced and patient in relationships.
It can. Like kunzite, some hiddenite loses colour in strong light and heat. Store it in a padded pouch away from windows, and charge it with moonlight rather than direct sun.
